annotatedSteps.description: Grouping terms and factorising into linear factors
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: × Sign error when factoring out of (−x + 3); it should be −1(x − 3)

annotatedSteps.description: Equating linear factors to zero to find the roots
annotatedSteps.studentWork:
2x + 1 = 0 or x − 3 = 0
x = −1/2 or x = 3
∴ roots are −1/2 and 3
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: ✓ Correctly solved the factors obtained (error carried forward)
annotatedSteps.correctedWorking:
2x − 1 = 0 or x − 3 = 0
x = 1/2 or x = 3
∴ roots are 1/2 and 3

teacherNote: Good job splitting the middle term and solving your linear factors correctly. Be careful with signs when grouping terms: factoring out from −x + 3 gives −1(x − 3), not +1(x − 3).

rubric.point: Equating factors to zero and finding the roots
